spec.goal: Make the toolset, not a prompt sentence, be what stops a judgment agent from writing. Audit every agent() call site in .claude/workflows/*.js, classify each as judgment (reads and reasons; must hold no Bash, Write or Edit) or write-permitted (legitimately needs shell/filesystem), bind every site to an agentType whose committed .claude/agents/*.md definition carries exactly the tools its class allows, add the read-only definitions that do not yet exist, unify the AT() helper across all nine workflows so it honors missing_agent_types per type rather than dropping every definition, and land a test that fails the moment a judgment call site regains an unbound (default workflow-subagent) toolset. The audit found 15 unbound sites: build-spec.js 3 (spec, route, decompose), build-implement.js 6 (three escalate, tiebreak, dispute, integrate:resolve), build-reentry.js 2 (classify, surfaces), create-project.js 2 (stack, seed), launch.js 1 (notes), maintain-triage.js 1 (incident); deploy.js, improve-analyze.js and memory-roll.js are already fully bound. Two sites are decided explicitly against reflex: build-spec's spec writer becomes read-only (Read/Glob/Grep, strong tier) because a node that runs npm test is doing the work rather than specifying it, and build-implement's integrate:resolve stays write-permitted at the strong tier via its own definition because binding it to the haiku-tier 'mechanical' type would silently downgrade the model. What each agent is asked to decide does not change: prompts gain only inline statements of the tool constraint (a dropped agentType takes its role prompt with it), and no label, model tier, schema or edge changes.

acceptance.given: the nine workflow scripts in .claude/workflows/ and the landed test
acceptance.when: the test scans each file for agent() option objects
acceptance.then: every option object names an agentType — literally, or through the workflow's AT()/NEW() helper — and the test fails with the file and the site's label for any option object that names none, so a site reverting to the default workflow-subagent toolset is a red test

acceptance.given: the set of agentType names referenced by all workflow call sites
acceptance.when: the test resolves each name against .claude/agents/
acceptance.then: every referenced name has a committed <name>.md whose frontmatter 'name' field equals its filename stem, and an unresolvable name fails the test naming the missing file

acceptance.given: each call site's resolved agent definition and its frontmatter 'tools' list
acceptance.when: the test checks whether that list contains Bash, Write or Edit
acceptance.then: the site passes only if it appears in an explicit WRITE_PERMITTED allowlist declared in the test file and keyed by workflow filename plus label pattern; any other site holding a write-capable type fails, so granting a judgment node a commit tool cannot land without editing the allowlist

acceptance.when: the test compares it against the sites actually present in the workflows
acceptance.then: it contains exactly the mechanical and write-legitimate sites — every AT('mechanical') site, the implementer, test-author, fixer, reproducer and patch-drafter sites, build-implement's integrate:resolve, and launch.js's release-notes 'notes' site — each carrying a one-line reason string; an allowlist entry that matches no site in any workflow also fails, so the list cannot rot

acceptance.given: build-spec.js, which today has no AT() helper and three unbound sites
acceptance.when: the test inspects its spec, route and decompose sites
acceptance.then: all three are bound through an AT() helper to agentTypes whose definitions carry exactly 'Read, Glob, Grep', the spec writer's definition is at the strong tier and grants no Bash, and no agent label 'planner' reappears (the plan-selection block between the existing sentinels is untouched)

acceptance.given: each call site's model option and its bound definition's frontmatter model
acceptance.when: the test maps MODEL.strong/mid/cheap to opus/sonnet/haiku and compares them
acceptance.then: the two agree at every site, so no binding silently re-tiers a node — in particular integrate:resolve is bound to a strong-tier write-capable definition rather than to the haiku-tier 'mechanical' type

acceptance.given: any workflow script and args carrying missing_agent_types: ['x'] for a type its runtime has not yet registered
acceptance.when: the workflow builds its agent options through AT()
acceptance.then: AT('x') yields {} while AT of every other type still yields { agentType: ... }, in all nine workflows including maintain-triage.js (whose NEW() helper folds into AT() while 'new_agent_types: false' keeps dropping exactly the four types it covered), and the test asserts each workflow's helper reads both A.agent_types and A.missing_agent_types

acceptance.given: a run whose args set agent_types: false
acceptance.when: any workflow builds its agent options
acceptance.then: every site's options object omits agentType, preserving the existing blunt hatch for a session that predates the definitions

acceptance.given: a judgment call site bound to a read-only type, whose role prompt disappears if the runtime has not yet registered that type
acceptance.when: the test reads the prompt text of each read-only-bound site
acceptance.then: the prompt itself states the read-only constraint inline (it must not create, edit or delete files, or run commands that change the repository), so the constraint survives a dropped agentType, and the existing instruction sentences describing WHAT to decide are preserved verbatim

acceptance.given: each new .claude/agents/*.md definition this work item adds
acceptance.then: a judgment definition lists tools exactly 'Read, Glob, Grep', names its model as one of opus/sonnet/haiku, and its body states the node's role and that it is read-only; the one new write-permitted definition (for integrate:resolve) states why it holds Bash, Write and Edit

acceptance.given: the historical pre-fix text of build-spec.js, in which the spec, route and decompose option objects carry no agentType, supplied as a string fixture
acceptance.when: the test's scanner — a pure function of workflow text plus a definitions map, reading nothing from disk at call time — is run over it
acceptance.then: it reports all three sites as unbound violations, demonstrating the guard failing on the shape that actually shipped rather than only passing on the fixed one, and the same scanner run over the fixed tree reports zero violations

acceptance.when: npm test is run from the repository root (node --test substrate/test/*.test.js)
acceptance.then: the whole suite passes, including the pre-existing plan-selection.test.js assertions that build-spec still spawns its judgment agents and spawns no 'planner'

acceptance.given: the workflow scripts before and after the change
acceptance.when: the set of agent() sites is compared by label pattern, model tier and schema name in each file
acceptance.then: the sets are identical — no agent() call is added, removed, re-labelled, re-tiered or given a different schema, and no pipeline/parallel/phase structure changes — so this work item alters only what each node is permitted to touch

out_of_scope: Changing what any agent is asked to decide: no prompt's decision content, rubric, schema, label, model tier or phase is altered; prompts gain only inline restatements of the tool constraint.
Converting any further agent into script code. The Iteration Planner is already replaced between the existing BEGIN/END plan-selection sentinels and that block is not touched here.
Re-tiering any node for cost (the dispute ruling stays mid, the Tiebreak Judge stays strong).
Path-level or directory-level sandboxing of a write-permitted agent: the granularity available is the frontmatter tools list, and narrowing writes to a directory is not attempted.
Edits to CLAUDE.md, COMPANY.md, OPERATING_MODEL.md, HANDOFF.md or backlog/venture0.json.
contracts.schema.json: no new or amended contract; this changes no edge shape.
substrate CLIs (artifacts.js, gates.js, ledger.js, validator.js, deploy.js) and every existing test file under substrate/test/ other than the new one.
The graph-lint and fix-loop blocks in build-spec.js and build-implement.js, beyond the option objects of their agent() calls.

Any runtime or harness change that would make an unknown agentType non-fatal; the missing_agent_types mechanism already in improve-analyze.js and memory-roll.js is the pattern to spread, not to redesign.
risk_reasons: No changes to stored data shapes or contracts (workflows produce identical outputs per AC-13)
No auth, secrets, payments, or deployed infrastructure touched; purely internal agent toolset configuration
Not irreversible; agent definitions and tests can be changed or rolled back if needed
No existing route contracts broken; AC-13 guarantees same inputs/outputs and no re-tiering or re-labeling
No external consumers affected (Venture 0 is self-contained; client is self)
Only internal scaffolding changes (workflow agent definitions, test files, agent capability bindings)
Preserves all existing decision logic and workflow behavior; changes only tool constraints, not prompts or structure
Additive safety and hygiene improvement to the build system itself

tasks.description: Create all 13 new agent type definitions in .claude/agents/ with correct frontmatter (tools, model tier) and role descriptions. Create read-only definitions (spec, route, decompose, escalate, tiebreak, dispute, classify, surfaces, stack, seed, incident) with tools=[Read, Glob, Grep] and inline statement that they are read-only. Create write-permitted definitions (integrate-resolve, notes) with tools=[Bash, Write, Edit, Read, Glob, Grep] and explanation of why they need write access. Ensure model tiers (strong=opus, mid=sonnet, cheap=haiku) match the guidance in CLAUDE.md and satisfy AC-6. Each definition body must state the agent's role and constraints inline to satisfy AC-9 and AC-10.

Add AT() helper function to each of the 9 workflow files. The AT(type) helper returns {} when agent_types===false or type is in missing_agent_types, otherwise returns {agentType:type}. Bind all 15 unbound agent() call sites via AT(): build-spec.js (spec, route, decompose), build-implement.js (escalate×3, tiebreak, dispute, integrate-resolve), build-reentry.js (classify, surfaces), create-project.js (stack, seed), launch.js (notes), maintain-triage.js (incident). Add inline constraint statements to workflow prompts where AT() binds to a read-only type (agent must not create, edit or delete files or run commands that change the repository). Verify agent() calls use the AT() option consistently and no other workflow structure changes (AC-13).

Implement substrate/test/agent-binding.test.js with comprehensive validation and substrate/test/agent-binding-helpers.js with reusable scanner/resolver functions. The test must: (1) scan all workflow files for agent() call sites and verify every option object names an agentType (AC-1, AC-11); (2) resolve each referenced agentType against .claude/agents/*.md and verify all exist with matching 'name' frontmatter (AC-2); (3) verify read-only sites have tools=[Read, Glob, Grep] and write sites are in WRITE_PERMITTED allowlist (AC-3); (4) verify WRITE_PERMITTED allowlist contains exactly: all AT('mechanical') sites, implementer/test-author/fixer/reproducer/patch-drafter sites, integrate-resolve, and notes, each with a reason string, and contains no orphaned entries (AC-4); (5) verify prompts of read-only sites state the constraint inline (AC-9); (6) test the scanner function against pre-fix historical build-spec.js text as a fixture, showing it detects violations (AC-11); (7) run npm test including existing plan-selection.test.js and verify all pass (AC-12); (8) verify model option in each workflow matches bound definition's model tier (AC-6).
